column1: # required_tools.tsv -- every tool a gate REFUSES without, one row per refusal site.
# Consumers install from this (gates/required_tools.py --repo . --install), never from a copy:
# a copied list drifts the day a gate gains a requirement (antiknob CI, 2026-10-05).
# tests/test_required_tools_manifest.py pins it to the code in both directions.
# Columns (TAB-separated): layer, tool, kind (brew|cargo|pip|system), install, site, floor.
# FLOOR, NEVER A PIN (G2b, 2026-10-25). `floor` is the OLDEST version a gate accepts; `-` is none
# (presence alone). A tool NEWER than its floor is green, always: the house runs the newest
# release of every layer, and an equality pin turned sys_updater's gate red on every goh release
# and toolchain update (owner: "why pin goh by version? The whole idea is to have ever improving
# qa gates"). goh_require / need / goh_py_require refuse a tool below it, by name, with both
# versions. One tool, one floor, on every row it has. Seeded from sys_updater's gate-floors.env
# (R3.29). Each floor's kind -- HARD (a feature below it does not exist) or PROVEN (the oldest
# version run green; lower it the day an older one is run green) -- and its reason:
#   python3 3.15         HARD, by owner ruling (G2d, 2026-10-25): the house interpreter is the newest
#                        RELEASE, and 3.15 is it. G2b set 3.9 here as "PROVEN: goh's own suite drives the
#                        gates on /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6, green" -- that recorded an ACCIDENT, not a
#                        decision: dozens of the suite's tests hand a gate PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, and every
#                        goh script ran a bare `python3`, so the gates under test ran on macOS's 3.9.6
#                        (EOL since 2025-10) while the suite itself ran on 3.15. The root is fixed, not
#                        the number alone: goh's scripts run "$GOH_PY", found by lib/house_python.sh (the
#                        newest python3 on PATH or in a release's install dirs, whatever the PATH order),
#                        and a machine whose newest is below this floor is refused, naming it. A repo's
#                        OWN pin (.python-version / GOH_PYTHON_VERSION) is judged against it too.
#   pytest 9.1.1         PROVEN: run green under 3.14 and 3.15.
#   zig 0.17.0           PROVEN: the C compiler cargo-zigbuild gives the musl lint configs.
#   shellcheck 0.11.0    PROVEN, and what goh shell_lint is calibrated against (two defects it
#                        exits 0 on are handled by goh, not by it).
#   cargo-machete 0.7.0  HARD: before it, ignored files (target/) were searched -- slow, and false
#                        "unused dependency" reports from generated sources.
#   cargo-audit 0.21.0   HARD: where version-4 Cargo.lock support landed (--deny unsound/yanked
#   cargo-zigbuild 0.24.0  PROVEN: cross-lints the two musl targets.
#   cargo-llvm-cov 0.6.24  HARD: `clean --profraw-only` is 0.6.12, and 0.6.24 fixed its
#                        "removes too many files" bug.
# A floor moves DOWN only with evidence and UP only in the commit whose code starts needing it.
